target_customer: Vehicle OEMs, dealers and dealer groups that sell titled vehicles online
problem: Franchise laws force new vehicle sales through licensed dealers, so manufacturers could not sell direct online in most states and compliance with titling, registration and taxes was hard.
business_model: Licensed dealer and software platform charging per transaction and subscriptions to OEMs and dealers

founders.name: Christopher Howard
education: Stanford, BS and MS in computer science (YC page)
founders.background_notes: From Atlanta and a published researcher per YC launch post.

founders.name: Rowan Mockler
founders.background_notes: From South Africa and a world champion public speaker per YC launch post.

competitors.name: ACERTUS
competitors.what: Vehicle title and registration processing, launched a platform API in June 2022

technical_complexity.rationale: Checkout, financing, insurance, titling and registration across states with dealer licensing; the hard parts are compliance logic per state and integrations.

defensibility.rationale: Dealer licenses and per-state compliance workflows are slow to build, and OEMs embed the checkout into their sites.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy or acquisition found; the current company site names Carvana as the threat to dealers.

market_need_then: YC launch post cites franchise laws, direct sale illegal for manufacturers in most states, and dealer commissions of 20 to 30 percent plus; EV makers wanted online sales.

branding.domain_note: Early contact address used ekhodealer.com; main site is ekho.com.

identity.visual_style: Clean modern product screenshots with a gradient design system per the site

rebrands.why: Not stated; company broadened from one product to a platform

brand_strength.rationale: Clear analogy positioning and named dealer case studies, but no independent press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Ekho began as Ekho Dealer, a licensed distribution layer letting OEMs sell online, and broadened into a platform for dealers and OEMs with an AI sales agent. It raised a 15M USD Series A led by Activant in July 2025 (17.3M total with seed) and remains active with about 30 people. Licensing and per-state compliance are the moat; scale beyond that is not yet shown.
notes: The company blog says 17.3M in total including a 15M Series A; the remaining 2.3M (seed) is implied, not stated, so no seed round is recorded; its date and investors are unknown. The Series A date is the announcement of 2025-07-08. Carvana appears only on the current site, not in a source dated at founding. The company site design uses gradients (not recorded as a brand fact). Name origin not found.
